questions.text: Why is Social Science described as a group of related disciplines rather than a single subject? Explain with the help of an example.
questions.answer_explanation: Human society is complex and no single field can fully explain it. For example, a drought affects crops (environment/Geography), farmers' incomes (Economics), government relief (Politics), and migration (Society). Different disciplines like Geography, History, Political Science, and Economics together provide a comprehensive understanding.

questions.text: Describe how wind erosion shapes the land surface. Name two landforms created by wind erosion.
questions.answer_explanation: Wind erosion occurs when strong winds pick up and transport loose sand and soil particles. These particles act as abrasives, wearing away rocks over time. Two landforms created by wind erosion are: (i) Mushroom rocks (or pedestal rocks) and (ii) Deflation hollows (or blowouts).

questions.text: Explain how the greenhouse effect helps in keeping the Earth warm. Name any two greenhouse gases.
questions.answer_explanation: The greenhouse effect is a natural process where certain gases in the Earth's atmosphere trap some of the Sun's heat. They allow sunlight to pass through but absorb and re-radiate the heat energy, preventing it from escaping back into space, thus keeping the planet warm. Two greenhouse gases are Carbon dioxide (CO²) and Methane (CH⁴).

questions.text: Describe the role of wind in the process of erosion and deposition, giving at least three examples of landforms created by each. (5 marks)
questions.or_alternative:
OR
Explain the various stages in the formation of a river valley from its source to its mouth, describing at least three major landforms created by a river in its course. (5 marks)
questions.answer_explanation:
Model Answer for Wind Erosion & Deposition:
- Wind erosion occurs through deflation (removal of loose particles) and abrasion (sandblasting of rocks).
- Erosional landforms include: (i) Mushroom rocks/pedestal rocks (narrow base formed by abrasion), (ii) Yardangs (streamlined ridges in soft rock), (iii) Desert pavement/lag deposits (deflation leaves behind coarse pebbles).
- Wind deposition occurs when wind speed drops, depositing sand and silt.
- Depositional landforms include: (i) Sand dunes (ridges/hills of sand - barchan, longitudinal), (ii) Loess plains (thick deposits of fine, fertile silt), (iii) Sand sheets (extensive flat areas of sand).
- The size of particles transported depends on wind velocity.
- Vegetation and obstacles influence dune shape and location.

questions.source_text: In a rural district of India, a severe drought has affected the lives of people in multiple ways. Due to lack of rainfall, crops have failed, leading to a sharp decline in farmers' incomes. The local government has stepped in to provide relief measures, such as subsidised food grains and work under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). This has prompted political discussions on the efficiency and reach of these schemes. As a result, many farming families have migrated to nearby cities in search of livelihood, altering the social structure of both the villages they left and the urban areas they joined. The community's traditional methods of conserving water and sharing resources, a part of their cultural heritage, are being revisited and discussed. Environmentalists are studying the changing patterns of the local climate and soil, while economists are analysing the impact on the regional economy. Historians are looking at how similar droughts were handled in the past and what lessons can be applied today. This single event of a drought, therefore, touches upon the environment, economy, politics, society, and culture, showing how different aspects of human life are deeply interconnected.
